svg.data-weight-note: 7.67 kg (16.91 lb), with two installed PSUs
svg.data-power-consumption: 1710 W maximum at both low and high line
svg.data-poe-budget: With a 30 W guard band - 750 W with one PSU, 1500 W with two, at both low and high line
svg.data-optics-sfp: Four 10G/25G SFP28 uplinks, ports 49-52. No per-cage breakout table is published, so none is stated here.
svg.data-optics-qsfp28: Two 100G QSFP28 ports, 53-54, sold as stacking ports and qualified by the datasheet itself - "stacking capability subject to NOS implementations".
svg.data-poe: All forty-eight RJ-45 ports support IEEE 802.3at and IEEE 802.3bt, up to 90 W per port depending on the budget. Cat 6 cabling, per the datasheet's prose. ONE CLASS ACROSS ALL FORTY-EIGHT, unlike the EPS203 which splits the same sockets by rate.

The EPS201 is the one that ships both and draws blue."},"gate-1":{"confidence":"borrowed","note":"THE FACE IS `edgecore/eps203`'s, AND THE EVIDENCE FOR THAT IS BETTER THAN THE EVIDENCE THIS DEVICE'S OWN ELEVATION COULD GIVE. Its own datasheet figures are the worst of the family. All four read between -3.7% and -6.2% on aspect against 438 x 43.7, and fitting the twenty-four RJ-45 column positions of its front elevation gives a straight-line rms of 0.695 mm with a quadratic term implying the local pitch GROWS 3.8% across the row - the opposite direction from the EPS201's -5.0%, and the same kind of fault. THE SHELL IS NOT SHARED AND THE FACE IS, which is the distinction that took the work. The chassis is 32 mm shallower and 0.3 mm lower than the EPS201's and EPS203's, so nothing could be assumed. But the three quick start guides turn out to share artwork, and the sharing is exact: this guide's button-and-lamp enlargement is BYTE-IDENTICAL to the EPS203's (md5 45c69467154e...), as are its PSU-replacement figure and the fan-tray figure all three carry. Its left-end port enlargement is NOT byte-identical - the port indicators are drawn white here and pale blue there - but registered against the EPS203's it needs ZERO pixels of shift, and the port aperture centres in the two come out at the same pixels to a tenth: 263.5, 422.0, 508.0 and 614.0 in both. Two renders of one face. A SCALE-FREE CHECK AGREES. The ratio of column pitch to jack aperture, which needs no calibration at all, reads 1.1778 on this guide's enlargement, 1.1778 on the EPS203's and 1.1776 on the EPS201's, against the 1.1814 the EPS203's measured geometry gives. AND THE HOMOGRAPHY TEST, WHICH PASSES FOR THE EPS201, FAILS HERE - which is worth recording because it is the test that would otherwise have been called decisive. Assuming this device's columns sit at the EPS203's positions, the best 1D perspective transform explains its datasheet elevation to only 0.484 mm rms, against 0.171 for the EPS201 and 0.069 for the EPS203 on itself; freeing the gutter ratio gets to 0.455 and wants a different one. THAT IS THIS FIGURE'S DISTORTION, NOT A DIFFERENT WALL - the two enlargements settle it - but a reader who only had the elevations would have concluded otherwise, and so would I have. EVERY FRONT-FACE FIGURE IN THIS FILE IS THE EPS203's, measured on its datasheet elevation at 2.2877 px/mm (24-column fit, rms 0.121 mm) and on its guide's enlargements at 7.5 to 10.0 px/mm."},"ports":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"Ports per the datasheet: 48 x 10/100/1000BASE-T, 4 x 10G/25G SFP28 uplinks and 2 x 100G QSFP28 stacking ports (whether stacking works depends on the NOS), with IEEE 802.3at and IEEE 802.3bt PoE on all 48 of the 10/100/1000BASE-T ports. ONE RATE AND ONE PoE CLASS, which is this model's own shape. The EPS201 on the same face has the same 48 x 1G and NO PoE; the EPS203 has the same 48 sockets split 36 at 2.5G and 12 at 10G with 90 W on all of them. Three machines, one port wall, three different answers to what comes out of it."},"power":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"\"2pcs 1+1 redundant, load-sharing, hot-swappable 1200W AC (80 PLUS Platinum compliant)\" - the same YPEB1200AM-1A03P10 the EPS203 takes, and its ordering table names both chassis: \"(for EPS202/AS4630-54PE, EPS203/AS4630-54NPE)\". Maximum power consumption \"Low-line: 1710 Watts High-line: 1710 Watts\" - the same figure at both lines, which is unusual enough to be worth quoting rather than paraphrasing - and a PoE budget with a 30 W guard band of \"750 W for 1 PSU/1500 W for 2 PSU\", again the same at both lines."},"the-height-nobody-can-resolve":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"THE PUBLISHED HEIGHT IS 43.7 AND THE SIBLINGS' IS 44.0, and the difference is 0.3 mm on figures whose finest pixel is 0.44. Both are roundings of inch values - this datasheet prints \"43.8 x 44.2 x 4.37 cm (17.24 x 17.40 x 1.72 in)\" and the siblings' print 1.73 in - and neither is 1RU's 44.45. `chassis.height` CARRIES 43.7 because that is what this device publishes, and every y figure on the face is the EPS203's, placed from the TOP edge. Nothing in any staged figure says whether the missing 0.3 mm comes off the top or the bottom, and at these resolutions nothing could."},"the-psu-hub-label-that-corrects-the-eps203":{"confidence":"measured","note":"THE SUPPLY'S FAN HUB IS PRINTED WITH THE SUPPLY'S WATTAGE, and this device is what proves it. Its rear elevation prints **\"2kV 1200W\"** on each hub, legible at 12x, and its supply is the 1200 W YPEB1200AM-1A03P10. THAT CORRECTS WHAT `edgecore/eps203` SAYS ABOUT THE SAME PART. The EPS203 takes the same supply - its ordering table names both chassis - and its rear elevation prints \"2kV 920W\" on the same hub. Faced with one drawing against three published statements of 1200 W, that file carried 1200 and explained the 920 as a figure belonging to the FAN rather than to the supply. The explanation was wrong: the label tracks the supply, and this second render of the same part shows it doing so. The conclusion was right for the wrong reason, which is worth saying out loud. SO WHAT THE EPS203'S \"920W\" IS is an inconsistency between two documents rendering one part, and the EPS203's provenance now says that instead. A photograph of a real YPEB1200AM's hub would say which render is stale."},"the-rear":{"confidence":"measured","note":"MEASURED ON THIS MODEL'S OWN REAR ELEVATION at 2.2763 px/mm, and it agrees with the EPS203's within the slack both figures carry. THREE FAN TRAY BAYS at x 47.0, 96.0 and 144.5 - a pitch of 48.75 against the EPS203's 48.15 and the EPS201's 48.1 - with the red handles reading 47.4-86.1, 96.6-134.9 and 145.9-183.2, widths 38.7, 38.2 and 37.3. The 2% spread in those widths is the figure's gradient, the same one the other two rears carry. TWO SUPPLY BAYS carrying the 1200 W module: its silver face reads 280.7-301.4 and 364.6-382.2 in the parts the mask catches, 83.9 apart, which is the EPS203's 84.0 pitch. The bays are drawn at the EPS203's measured 270.0 and 354.0 because that figure resolves their edges and this one does not."},"the-shallower-shell":{"confidence":"datasheet","note":"438 x 442 x 43.7 against the EPS201's and EPS203's 438 x 474 x 44. THIRTY-TWO MILLIMETRES IS NOT A ROUNDING, and the issue that scoped this work says so in as many words. What it does not change is the face: the rear is the EPS203's too - same three fan-tray bays on the same pitch, same two 1200 W supplies on the same 84 mm pitch - and the depth goes somewhere neither elevation shows. THE RACK KIT NAMES ALL THREE ANYWAY: \"RKIT-100G-SLIDE ... For EPS200 series/AS4630-54TE/54PE/54NPE\". A slide kit that fits a 442 mm and a 474 mm chassis is a statement about the rails, not about the boxes."}},"references":[{"title":"Edgecore AS4630-54PE Quick Start Guide"},{"title":"Edgecore EPS202 / AS4630-54PE Enterprise Switch Datasheet"}],"version":"1.0.1","views":{"bottom":{"empty":"Not drawn by any staged source.
